reasons: Covers each callout mode, label choice, priority, activity fallback, and placement rules.
Each test has a clear expected result.
The fake data is simplified, so it does not prove behavior with full real files.

terms.meaning: the test runner that runs these checks and reports which ones pass or fail
made-up sample data built for a test
the thin line joining a schedule card to its element

used_by: Run by the test runner, not imported by app code

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports
sections.what: Brings in the test functions, the types for activities and elements, and the three callout functions being checked.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the usual pattern for a test file.

sections.name: component
sections.title: Made-up element builder
sections.what: Creates a fake element with a given id, dates and list of linked activity ids, with the other fields filled in as placeholders.
sections.why: Tests need realistic-looking inputs without loading a real model file.
sections.watch_out: The fake skips many real fields, so a bug caused by a missing real field would not appear in these tests.

sections.name: story
sections.title: Made-up activity builder
sections.what: Creates a fake schedule activity with a code, a name and dates.
sections.why: Gives the callout rules the activity details they show on cards.
sections.watch_out: The types are loosened on purpose, so a wrong field name here would not be flagged by the compiler.

sections.name: components
sections.title: Three sample elements
sections.what: Defines three sample elements: one finished, one in progress with four activities, and one planned for later.
sections.why: Covers complete, active and future states in a single set of data.
sections.watch_out: The dates are fixed, so the sample only tests the chosen test date.

sections.name: stories
sections.title: Six sample activities
sections.what: Defines six sample activities with codes and names, which the sample elements link to.
sections.why: Gives the cards readable activity text to check.
sections.watch_out: The names are chosen for readability and are not taken from a real schedule.

sections.name: everything
sections.title: Shared test values
sections.what: Holds a set containing all sample element ids and a fixed test date of 15 February 2026.
sections.why: A fixed date makes the in-progress tests give the same result every run.
sections.watch_out: If the sample dates change, the chosen test date may no longer fall where these tests expect.

sections.name: schedule callouts (part 1)
sections.title: Checks label choice and priority
sections.what: Checks that active mode shows only work in progress with the right activity first, that a selected element comes first, that all mode lists by priority, and that off mode shows nothing. It also checks that pinned labels survive every mode except off, that hidden labels are dropped, and that the element name omits the phase suffix.
sections.why: These are the user-facing choices that decide which labels appear.
sections.watch_out: The off mode test drops pinned labels as well, which conflicts with the comment in the callouts module that says pinned labels always show.

sections.name: schedule callouts (part 2)
sections.title: Checks activity fallback
sections.what: Checks that when no activity record is available, the card shows the raw activity id with an empty name.
sections.why: Schedules can refer to activities that are missing from the file, and the card must still show something.
sections.watch_out: The name is blank, so the card shows only the id.

sections.name: callout placement
sections.title: Checks card placement on screen
sections.what: Checks that a card is placed above and to the right of its element first, moves to another side when that spot is taken, returns nothing when every spot is blocked, stays inside the screen, and joins the leader line at the nearest card edge.
sections.why: These rules keep cards readable and on screen.
sections.watch_out: The checks use one fixed screen size, so behavior on very small or very large screens is not covered.

summary: Tests that the schedule callout rules pick the right labels, order them by priority, keep user choices, and place cards on screen.
purpose: Protects the behavior of the callout module so label changes do not quietly break what users see.
why: Likely reason: the callout rules have several interacting modes and priorities, which are easy to break without tests.
how: Builds small made-up elements and activities, runs the callout builder in each mode, and checks the output. It then checks the placement and leader line functions against fixed screen sizes.
inputs: Made-up elements, schedule activities, a fixed test date of 15 February 2026, and fixed screen sizes.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the Vitest test runner.
risks: The fixed date means changing date behavior is not covered. The fake elements skip many real fields, so missing real fields would not be caught.
debug: Run the test file alone and read the failing expectation. Compare the output list order against the priority rules in the callouts module. Check that the sample dates still fall in the expected states.
